video_metadata.working_title: VERMONT 1971 Cold Case — DNA Identified Her Killer After 51 Years | Rita Curran
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: Rita Curran, a 24-year-old second-grade teacher from Milton, was killed in her Burlington, Vermont apartment in July 1971; for decades rumor pointed at Ted Bundy, but in February 2023 Burlington police announced that DNA on a cigarette butt left beside her body identified William DeRoos, the man who lived two floors above her, who died in 1986 and was never charged.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: Grief for a young teacher, unease that the answer was a few steps away all along, quiet anger at a false alibi kept for five decades, and a bittersweet sense of truth arriving too late for trial.

protagonist._instructions: Antagonist of the story. Never convicted, never charged. Strict legal wording: identified by DNA, according to Burlington police.
protagonist.age_at_time_of_events: 31 (born December 14, 1939, in Chicago, Illinois, per a July 28, 1971 Burlington police entry quoted in the 2023 Trieb report) [8]
protagonist.occupation_or_status: Tenant in the same Brookes Avenue building as Rita Curran, living in a third-floor apartment (listed in the police report as 15 Brookes Ave) with his then-wife Michelle [8][2]. Never charged; died in 1986.
protagonist.location: Burlington, Vermont (1971); later Thailand; later San Francisco, California, where he died on August 7, 1986 [13][1]
protagonist.physical_description: Not documented in the sources consulted; do not describe.
protagonist.background_brief: According to Burlington police, after the murder DeRoos left Burlington, went to Thailand and became a Buddhist monk, later turned up in San Francisco, where he met another wife, and died there in 1986 of a drug overdose (acute morphine poisoning) in a hotel room [2][13][1]. Some reports say he had a criminal record [1]; later reporting describes a history of violence toward a later wife (single-sourced, see notes) [13].
protagonist.psychological_profile: Not to be speculated. Documented behaviour only: according to police, he told officers in 1971 he had been home with his wife all night and persuaded her to back that alibi [1][2].
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: He smoked; a Lark brand cigarette butt found beside Rita's right arm carried the DNA that police say was his [11].
protagonist.nickname_or_alias_if_any: None documented. His wife's name is spelled Michelle (most reports) and 'Michele' in the police report excerpt [1][8].

individuals.name: Rita Curran
individuals.role_or_profession: Second-grade teacher at Milton Elementary School in Milton, Vermont; summer job as a chambermaid at a Burlington motel (named in some reports as the Colonial Motor Inn) [1][16]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Downstairs neighbor in the same building; according to the Trieb report they did not appear to have known each other [1][8]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Beaten, sexually assaulted and strangled in her ground-floor bedroom on the night of July 19–20, 1971; she was 24 [1][2][20]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Eldest of three children, with a brother Thomas three years younger and a sister Mary five years younger; attended Trinity College in Burlington; her family home was in Milton (single-sourced podcast account) [16]

individuals.name: Tom (Thomas) Curran
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Lost his older sister at about 21; waited more than five decades for an answer
individuals.humanizing_detail: Spoke at the February 21, 2023 press conference; said he thinks less about the killer than about Rita and his parents, and that he prays to his parents and to Rita (paraphrase) [9][7]
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: Paraphrase only; no verified verbatim quote.

individuals.name: Mary Curran Campbell
individuals.role_or_profession: Rita's younger sister, of Hartland, Vermont
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Often wondered if her sister's killer would ever be identified; spoke at the 2023 press conference [10][9]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Later spoke with Senator Patrick Leahy about the case, per the Vermont Standard [10]

collective_victims_if_applicable.group_description: Rita's parents (who died without an answer), siblings, roommates who found her, her Milton pupils and the Burlington community
collective_victims_if_applicable.range_of_impacts: Grief, fear in a small city, decades of rumor including the Ted Bundy theory

characters.name: Jon Murad
characters.role_in_story: Acting chief of the Burlington Police Department in February 2023
characters.notable_quotes: "The random violence of her murder left a stain on our community and it devastated her family." [6][20]; on the wife: "Five decades later, she gave our detectives a different story: the truth." [9]; DeRoos "moved to Thailand and became a Buddhist monk" [13]

characters.name: Lt. James Trieb
characters.role_in_story: Commander of the Burlington Police Detective Services Bureau; author of the 34-page final report
characters.key_actions_they_took: Led the cold case review and wrote the report released in February 2023 [8]
characters.notable_quotes: Said the detective bureau and the chief were confident that William DeRoos was responsible for the aggravated murder of Rita Curran, and that because he died of an overdose he would not be held accountable (paraphrase of press reports) [2][7]

characters.name: CeCe Moore
characters.role_in_story: Chief genetic genealogist at Parabon NanoLabs
characters.key_actions_they_took: Traced the cigarette-butt DNA profile through open-source genealogy databases to DeRoos [4]
characters.notable_quotes: "This case is over 50 years old, and it only took a few hours to narrow it down to William DeRoos." [4]

characters.name: Sarah George
characters.key_actions_they_took: Reviewed the evidence and found probable cause for aggravated first-degree murder had DeRoos been alive [6][1]
characters.notable_quotes: "I would have felt perfectly comfortable going to trial." [7]

characters.name: Michelle DeRoos
characters.key_actions_they_took: Backed her husband's alibi in 1971; told the 1971 detective she had not heard or seen anything [8]; decades later told detectives he had left their apartment for a brief period that night [9]
characters.notable_quotes: None verbatim; described through police statements.

characters.name: Detective Winterbottom
characters.key_actions_they_took: Spoke with Mrs. DeRoos in 1971, per the Trieb report [8]

characters.name: Roommates (one named Lamphere in press accounts)
characters.role_in_story: Shared the Brookes Avenue apartment; found Rita
characters.key_actions_they_took: Returned after an evening out and found her on the bedroom floor in the early hours of July 20, 1971 [1][21]

characters.name: DeRoos's half-brother (unnamed)
characters.key_actions_they_took: Voluntarily gave a DNA sample; analysis indicated a 97 percent probability he and the cigarette donor were half-siblings [2][8]

characters.name: Ted Bundy
characters.role_in_story: Rumored suspect, never linked by evidence
characters.key_actions_they_took: Born in Burlington in 1946; named in theories by authors and a retired FBI agent; denied involvement to FBI agent William Hagmaier on January 22, 1989 [1][14]

events.what_happened: Ted Bundy is born at the Elizabeth Lund Home for Unwed Mothers.
events.significance: Origin of the later rumor linking Bundy to the case.

events.what_happened: Rita Curran teaches second grade at Milton Elementary School.
Rita works as a motel chambermaid and shares a ground-floor apartment on Brookes Avenue with roommates; the DeRoos couple live two floors above.
Rita's roommates are out; DeRoos, according to police, leaves his apartment after an argument with his wife to 'cool down'.
Rita Curran, 24, is beaten, sexually assaulted and strangled. A Lark cigarette butt is left beside her right arm.
events.significance: The cigarette is the evidence that matters 51 years later.

events.date: Early hours of Tuesday, July 20, 1971 (reports say about 12:30 a.m. or 1:20 a.m.)
events.what_happened: Roommates return and find Rita dead on her bedroom floor.
Police canvass the building; DeRoos says he was home all night with his wife; she says she heard and saw nothing.
A police record entry lists William DeRoos, age 31, of 15 Brookes Ave, DOB 12-14-39, born in Chicago.
events.significance: He was in the file from the start but, per the 2023 report, never treated as a person of interest.

events.what_happened: According to police, DeRoos leaves Burlington, goes to Thailand and becomes a Buddhist monk.
events.significance: Flight; his wife kept the alibi.

events.what_happened: Ted Bundy, later revealed as a serial killer, is rumored as a suspect because he was born in Burlington; a retired FBI agent, John Bassett, later proposes him; no evidence ever links him.
events.significance: A dead end that consumed attention.

events.what_happened: DeRoos dies of acute morphine poisoning (drug overdose), aged 46, never charged.
On the eve of his execution, Bundy denies involvement in the Curran case to FBI agent William Hagmaier.
Burlington police send crime-scene evidence including the cigarette butt for DNA analysis; a profile is developed but matches no one in criminal databases.
A new team of detectives renews the investigation.
Police contract Parabon NanoLabs; genealogist CeCe Moore traces the profile to DeRoos within hours, via relatives on both paternal and maternal sides.

A living half-brother gives DNA (97 percent half-sibling probability); DNA on Rita's torn housecoat matches the cigarette profile; DeRoos's former wife tells detectives he had left their apartment that night.
Acting Chief Jon Murad, Lt. James Trieb, CeCe Moore and State's Attorney Sarah George announce DeRoos as the man identified by DNA; Tom Curran and Mary Curran Campbell speak; the case is closed.
Case closed by Burlington police; no charges possible; no further public developments found.

the_moment.exact_location: Ground-floor apartment, Brookes Avenue, Burlington, Vermont
the_moment.what_is_happening: Roommates come home and find Rita Curran, 24, dead in her bedroom; a cigarette butt lies beside her arm.
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: The man police now say killed her lived two floors up and told police that morning he had been home all night.
the_moment.ironic_twist: The city whispered about Ted Bundy for decades; the answer was a neighbor whose wife gave him an alibi, and the evidence was a cigarette butt kept in storage for half a century.

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: Who killed a young teacher in her own bedroom while her roommates were out, and why did it take 51 years to name him?

the_method.technique_name: Investigative genetic genealogy (IGG) plus kinship DNA confirmation
step_by_step_explanation: The cigarette butt kept since 1971 is tested; a DNA profile is developed in 2014 but matches no one in criminal databases [1][4].
In 2022 Parabon NanoLabs is contracted; the DNA is used in open-source genealogy databases where people upload their own DNA [4].
Partial matches with distant relatives on both paternal and maternal sides are found [2].
CeCe Moore builds family trees and narrows the candidate to William DeRoos within hours [4].
A living half-brother voluntarily provides DNA; analysis gives a 97 percent probability of half-siblinghood with the cigarette donor [2][8].
DNA on Rita's torn housecoat is found to match the cigarette DNA [2][7].
DeRoos's former wife tells detectives he had left the apartment for a period that night [9].
the_method.why_it_worked: The cigarette butt was preserved for five decades and genealogy databases had grown large enough to find relatives.

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: A national index that only finds people already in the system, like a phone book of offenders.
Using DNA shared with cousins who uploaded their profiles to build a family tree backward and forward until one person fits.
Comparing a known relative's DNA with the evidence to measure how likely they share one parent.

the_method.scale_of_operation: A few hours of tree-building after 51 years of waiting [4].

systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: The 1971 investigation (Burlington Police Department), and the limits of forensic science at the time
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: The neighbor's alibi was accepted; per the 2023 report, DeRoos was never investigated as a person of interest in 1971; DNA testing did not exist; attention drifted to rumors such as Bundy.
specific_incompetence_examples: DeRoos was interviewed the day the body was found and recorded in a July 28, 1971 entry, yet never treated as a suspect [8].
His wife's alibi was not broken for about 51 years [9].
He was able to leave the country for Thailand [13].
The first DNA profile was developed only in 2014, 43 years later [1][4].
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The killer, according to police, lived in the same building; he was added to the DNA comparison pool in recent years only 'because of his proximity to this crime' [8].

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Burlington Police Department, Detective Services Bureau
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: Neighbor alibi accepted; Ted Bundy rumor never supported by evidence.
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: Genetic genealogy by Parabon NanoLabs in 2022 on the cigarette DNA.
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: Leaving a cigarette butt beside the body.
the_investigation.how_long_until_caught: Never caught; identified about 51 years and 7 months later, after his death.

the_confrontation.scene_description: Police, the state's attorney, the genealogist and Rita's brother and sister speak publicly; the case is declared closed.
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: The man he left behind, his wife, was the one who finally told the truth.

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: Paraphrase: he thinks less about the killer than about Rita and his parents, and prays to them.
victim_impact_statements.emotional_impact: Faith and grief rather than anger.

legal_resolution.sentence_received: None. State's Attorney Sarah George said there was probable cause for aggravated first-degree murder had he been alive.
legal_resolution.current_status: DeRoos was never charged or convicted; he died in 1986. Burlington police closed the case in February 2023. No later developments found as of October 2026.

details: The infamous serial killer born in Burlington was the rumor; the answer was the quiet neighbor upstairs.
The man police say killed her was questioned the same day, and his wife's word was enough.
A man who, according to police, had strangled a young teacher went to Thailand and became a Buddhist monk.
The truth came from the same woman who had covered for him, five decades later.

key_locations.atmosphere: Summer, college town between semesters (general context)
key_locations.relevant_details: Rita shared one of two ground-floor bedrooms with a roommate [1][20][8]

universal_stakes.why_this_matters_to_viewer: Danger may be close and familiar; a single preserved object can speak decades later.
universal_stakes.how_this_could_happen_to_them: A neighbor in the same building, an alibi from a spouse, a rumor that pulled attention elsewhere.
universal_stakes.lesson_or_warning: Keep the evidence; question convenient alibis; rumors are not evidence.
universal_stakes.current_relevance: Genetic genealogy continues to identify killers in very old cases, often after their deaths.
